# Dr. Stacy Peck, DACM, L.Ac.

> Dr. Stacy Peck is a Doctor of Acupuncture and Chinese Medicine, licensed acupuncturist, author and educator. She writes plain-language Chinese medicine books and guides for everyday readers, and the Herbal Rhymes mnemonic study system for the NCBAHM (formerly NCCAOM) and CALE acupuncture board exams. This site is her author hub and shop.

Books are sold by Amazon in paperback and Kindle. Guides and study tools are instant PDF downloads; checkout runs through Gumroad on the shop page, and the same items are listed on Etsy. Digital downloads are not refundable. Content is educational and is not medical advice.

## Books for everyday readers
- [Your Body Is Trying to Tell You Something](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GHPV8GVD?tag=herbalrhymes-20): how Chinese medicine reads common signals such as sleep, digestion, energy and stress, with food and daily-habit guidance. Paperback and Kindle. Comes with free [7-Day Kickstart Meal Plans](https://drstacypeck.com/meal-plans).
- [What Would Your Acupuncturist Say?](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GTFMDSDQ?tag=herbalrhymes-20): an A-to-Z guide to what Chinese medicine says about everyday health questions. Paperback and Kindle.

## Books for TCM students
- [Herbal Rhymes: Single Herbs Edition](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GTRLRX4Z?tag=herbalrhymes-20): rhyming mnemonics for 217 single herbs.
- [Herbal Rhymes: Formulas Edition](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GHQB5S9R?tag=herbalrhymes-20): rhyming mnemonics for 128 formulas.

## Articles: Chinese medicine for everyday life
- [Itchy, Dry Skin the Minute the Heat Comes On? Chinese Medicine Explains (and What to Do)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/itchy-dry-skin-winter-heat-chinese-medicine): Why skin itches when the furnace turns on: Blood deficiency generating Wind in Chinese medicine, verified against the Suwen and Maciocia. Foods, 3 acupressure points (SP 10, LI 11, SP 6), and a 6-week plan.
- [Dry Skin, a Dry Cough, and a Heavy Heart: Why Autumn Brings All Three (and the One Organ Behind Them)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/dry-skin-dry-cough-grief-lung-tcm): Why dry skin, a tickly cough and autumn sadness show up together: the Lung system in Chinese medicine, verified against the Neijing and Maciocia, with a 14-day inside-out plan.
- [Clocks Fall Back on November 1: Why You’ll Sleep Worse This Week (and the 2,000-Year-Old Fix)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/clocks-fall-back-sleep-chinese-medicine): Daylight saving ends Nov 1, 2026. What the Huangdi Neijing says about autumn and winter sleep, why the clock change wrecks your week, and 4 acupressure points (Kidney 6, Bladder 62, PC 6, HT 7) for the transition.
- [Acupressure for Sleep: 5 Points That Actually Help](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/acupressure-for-sleep): Can&rsquo;t sleep? A licensed acupuncturist shares 5 acupressure points for falling asleep faster and the 3am wake-up rescue &mdash; free steps you can try tonight.
- [Why You Always Get Sick in October (TCM Explains)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/sick-in-october-tcm): Why October is the hardest month for your immune defenses: wei qi, wind invasion, and dryness — what your fall cold means and how to protect yourself.
- [What Chinese Medicine Says About the Fall-to-Winter Transition](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/fall-winter-transition-tcm): Chinese medicine explains the fall-to-winter shift — Metal to Water, Lung to Kidney — plus what to eat, which acupressure points to press, and how to move through it.
- [Why Fall Makes You Sad: What Chinese Medicine Says About Grief and the Lungs](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/fall-lung-grief-tcm): Feeling weepy every autumn? In Chinese medicine, fall is Metal season — the Lungs — and its emotion is grief. Why the season stirs sadness and what helps.
- [5 TCM Rituals for the Season Change](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/5-tcm-season-change-rituals): Five small rituals from Chinese medicine for the fall-to-winter transition: warm mornings, the scarf rule, earlier nights, seasonal eating, and letting go.
- [The Real Reason You Can't Sleep: Chinese Medicine's Approach to Insomnia](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/insomnia-chinese-medicine): Chinese medicine treats insomnia by identifying the root pattern — not just prescribing a sedative. Learn the TCM approach to sleeplessness, including acupressure and food therapy.
- [Stress, Anxiety, and Overthinking: What Chinese Medicine Understands That Western Medicine Misses](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/anxiety-stress-chinese-medicine): Chinese medicine sees anxiety, stress, and overthinking as distinct patterns with different root causes — and treats the root, not just the symptom.
- [Why You're Always Hot (Or Always Cold): What Chinese Medicine Says About Your Internal Thermostat](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/always-hot-always-cold-chinese-medicine): Chinese medicine explains why some people always run hot and others can't get warm — Yin deficiency, Yang deficiency, and what to do about it.
- [Why You Keep Waking Up at 3am (According to Chinese Medicine)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/waking-up-at-3am-chinese-medicine): The TCM organ clock explains why so many people wake up between 1 and 3am — what Liver time means and what to do about it.
- [What Your Tongue Is Telling You About Your Health: A TCM Guide](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/tongue-diagnosis-tcm-guide): A practical guide to TCM tongue diagnosis: what color, coating, shape, and texture reveal about your health.
- [Chinese Medicine Food Therapy: What to Eat for Your Body Type](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/tcm-food-therapy-body-type): TCM food therapy explained — learn whether you run hot, cold, damp, or dry and which foods support your constitution.
- [5 Signs You Have Qi Deficiency (And What to Do About It)](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/qi-deficiency-symptoms): The 5 key signs of Qi deficiency in Chinese medicine and practical strategies — food therapy, acupressure, and lifestyle changes — to rebuild your energy.
- [The Chinese Medicine Body Clock: What Your Body Does Every 2 Hours](https://drstacypeck.com/blog/chinese-medicine-body-clock): The complete 24-hour TCM organ clock with practical advice for every two-hour window — meal timing, sleep, exercise, and more.
